title: Himachal seasons and altitude, month by month
meta_description: When to visit Himachal: month-by-month weather for Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala and Kinnaur, monsoon road risks, snow months and altitude advice.
summary: The best months for most of Himachal are April to mid-June and late September to November. July and August bring monsoon landslides; December to February brings snow to Shimla and Manali and closes the high villages of Kinnaur. Most places in this hive sit between 1,000 and 3,000 m, so altitude is rarely a problem.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Himachal has four travel seasons, and the right one depends on where you are going and what you want. Spring, from March to mid-June, brings blossom in the orchards, long days and busy hill stations. The monsoon, from July to mid-September, turns the hills green but makes roads unreliable. Autumn, from late September to November, has the clearest skies of the year. Winter, from December to February, brings snow to Shimla and Manali and quiet to everywhere else.

Height changes everything. Chamba sits at about 1,000 m and is warm in May; Chitkul, at about 3,450 m, is cold even in June and is often cut off by snow from December to March. The table below gives a quick view; the sections that follow explain the details. Weather is changing, and recent years have brought heavy rain events outside the usual months, so always check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Spring: March to mid-June
paras: Spring starts low and moves up the hills. In March, rhododendrons flower red in the forests around Shimla and McLeodganj, and Bir's paragliding season begins. By April, apple and pear blossom covers the orchards of Kullu, Naggar and Kinnaur, and the Tirthan valley turns green. Days in Manali are around 15–25 °C, nights cool.

From mid-May to June, schools in the plains close and families head to Shimla and Manali. This is the busiest and most expensive time on the main circuit, with traffic jams on the Manali road and room rates up to double. Go to Kinnaur, the Tirthan valley or Chamba instead, or travel in April and early May. Rohtang Pass usually opens to vehicles around May; the Atal tunnel stays open most of the year. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Monsoon: July to mid-September
paras: The south-west monsoon hits the outer hills hardest. McLeodganj and Dharamshala are among the wettest places in India, and the Kangra valley gets heavy, steady rain. The Kullu valley and Shimla also get frequent downpours. Landslides close roads for hours or days, especially the Mandi–Kullu gorge, the Parvati valley road, the Chamba roads and NH5 in Kinnaur. Flash floods on the Beas and its tributaries have caused serious damage in recent years.

For these reasons we do not run road trips in July and August. If you must travel, keep plans short and flexible, stay near main towns, avoid riverside rooms and travel in daylight. The rewards are green slopes, waterfalls and low prices. Chamba's Minjar Mela falls in this season, and Kinnaur, in the rain shadow, gets less rain than the outer hills, though its roads are still affected by slides lower down.
list: Keep a buffer day before any flight or train.
Watch the India Meteorological Department's district warnings.
Do not cross swollen streams on foot.
Choose rooms away from riverbanks during heavy rain.

sections.heading: Autumn: late September to November
paras: Autumn is our favourite season. The rain clears, the air is dry and the views of the Dhauladhar, Pir Panjal and Kinnaur Kailash ranges are sharpest. Apples are harvested in September and October in Kullu, Shimla's upper hills and Kinnaur, and the Baspa valley turns gold. Kullu Dussehra, usually in October, fills the Kullu valley with village deities and visitors.

Days are pleasant, around 15–22 °C in Manali in October, but nights get cold quickly; Kalpa and Sangla drop near freezing by November. Diwali brings a short spike in prices. By late November, homestays in Chitkul start to close and the high villages empty out.

sections.heading: Winter: December to February
paras: Winter in Himachal means snow for those who want it and quiet for those who do not. Shimla, Manali and the hills above McLeodganj often get snowfall between late December and February, and Solang near Manali is the main snow area. The Atal tunnel to Lahaul can close after heavy snow. Kinnaur stays reachable on NH5 most of the time, but Chitkul and side roads are often blocked, and many homestays close.

Roads to the main towns are kept open, but black ice is common in the mornings and snow can stop traffic for a day or two. Carry warm layers, gloves and good shoes, and leave buffer time. Chamba and the lower Kangra valley are mild in winter and make a good choice if you want the hills without the cold.

sections.heading: Matching the season to your trip
paras: The calendar matters more for some trips than others. A hill-station holiday in Shimla works almost all year except in heavy monsoon weeks, while a Kinnaur road trip has two good windows, May to June and September to October. Treks such as Triund, Kheerganga and the walks in the Great Himalayan National Park are best in April to June and October to November, when trails are dry and views clear; in winter, snow and ice make the higher sections dangerous without proper gear and a guide.

Festivals can also set the date. Losar in McLeodganj falls in February or March, Chamba's Minjar Mela in late July or early August, and Kullu Dussehra in October. All follow lunar calendars, so dates shift every year. If a festival is the reason for your trip, book rooms early, as towns fill quickly, and confirm the dates with the organisers or state tourism before you pay.
list: Honeymoons: March–April or October–November for quiet hotels and clear weather
Families: April and October avoid both the heat of the plains and the crowds of June
Snow: January and early February in Shimla and Manali
Photography: October for sharp air, November for autumn colour in Kinnaur

sections.heading: Altitude: what to expect
paras: Most of this hive is low enough that altitude sickness is not a real concern. Shimla is at about 2,200 m, Manali about 2,050 m and McLeodganj about 2,080 m. Kalpa, at about 2,960 m, and Sangla, about 2,700 m, are where some visitors notice it: a mild headache, poor sleep or breathlessness on stairs on the first night.

Day trips go higher. Chitkul is at about 3,450 m, Jalori Pass and Sissu about 3,100 m, and Rohtang Pass 3,978 m. Short visits are usually fine for healthy people, but move slowly, drink water and come down if symptoms get worse. Anyone with heart or lung conditions, and pregnant travellers, should talk to their doctor before going above 3,000 m.
list: Sleep below 3,000 m in this hive; visit higher places by day.
Take the first evening easy after arriving in Kalpa or Sangla.
Avoid alcohol on the first night at height.
Descend if headache, nausea or confusion worsen.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Himachal?
faqs.a: October is the best single month for most travellers: clear skies, mountain views, apple season and Kullu Dussehra. April and May are also excellent for blossom and pleasant days. Avoid July and August for road trips because of landslides.

faqs.q: When does it snow in Manali and Shimla?
faqs.a: Snowfall usually comes between late December and February, with January the most likely month. It varies from year to year, and some winters bring little snow to the towns. For a near-certain snow day, head to Solang or the Atal tunnel area above Manali.

faqs.q: Is it safe to visit Himachal in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It is risky for road travel. Landslides and flash floods close roads, and serious damage has occurred in recent monsoons. If you go, stay flexible, avoid riverside rooms and check current status before you travel. We do not run road trips then.

faqs.q: Will I get altitude sickness in Himachal?
faqs.a: Unlikely on the main circuit, which stays below about 2,200 m. In Kalpa and Sangla, near 3,000 m, some people get a mild headache on the first night. Day trips to Chitkul or Rohtang go higher; move slowly and talk to your doctor if you have health conditions.

NH5 to Reckong Peo and Kalpa usually stays open, but snow can block it for a day or two. Chitkul and side roads are often closed, and many homestays shut from December to March. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is apple season in Himachal?
faqs.a: Apples are harvested from about August to October, starting in the lower orchards and ending in Kinnaur. September and early October are the best time to see orchards heavy with fruit.

faqs.q: Is Himachal crowded in May and June?
faqs.a: Shimla and Manali are very crowded during the school holidays, with traffic jams and high room rates. Choose Kinnaur, Tirthan, Chamba or Bir instead, or travel in April.

faqs.q: When is the paragliding season in Bir?
faqs.a: The main seasons are March to May and October to November, when winds are steady and skies clear. Flying stops in the monsoon. Rules and dates change; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Himachal in October?
faqs.a: Light layers for the day, a warm jacket, fleece and cap for the evenings, good walking shoes and sunscreen. In Kinnaur, add thermals; nights in Kalpa and Sangla can drop near freezing by late October.
